back: A list of all ledger balances at a date, debits in one column and credits in the other, used to check the arithmetical accuracy of the double entry.
Debit balances: Expenses, Assets, Drawings. Credit balances: Liabilities, Income, Capital.

front: Four purposes of a trial balance
back: Check arithmetical accuracy; help locate errors; summarise the ledger balances; provide the basis for the financial statements.

front: Main limitation of a trial balance
back: Agreement does not prove the books are correct: six types of error (omission, commission, principle, original entry, complete reversal, compensating) leave the totals equal.

front: Which inventory is in the trial balance?
back: Opening inventory (a debit). Closing inventory is shown as a note below the trial balance.
Returns inwards (sales returns): debit. Returns outwards (purchases returns): credit.
Discount allowed (an expense): debit. Discount received (income): credit.
Capital = total debit balances − all other credit balances.

front: Effect of a balance in the wrong column
back: It creates a difference of twice the amount between the totals.
